verdict.rationale: Granola documents private-by-default notes: a note is shared only when you copy its link or add it to a team-space folder. It also documents a private 'My notes' space alongside a workspace team space whose folders everyone in the workspace can see. However, nothing shows granular permission levels on links or folders, or any admin view of what has been shared. The only admin-related signal is an 'audit' endpoint listed in the OpenAPI spec, with no description of what it covers. Missing for 10: granular link/folder permission levels (view/edit, restricted or external links), documented admin visibility or controls over shared notes, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an IT admin, sharing is controlled — private-by-default notes, granular link/folder/workspace permissions, and admin visibility into what's shared

citations.quote: Your notes are never shared with any participants unless you share the link, or add the note to a folder in your team space.
The Granola sidebar is organized into two spaces: My notes — Your private space... [Your workspace name] — Your team space.
Folders here are visible to everyone in your workspace.
Copy link will copy a unique URL link to the meeting notes, which you can send to others.
